The NCATS variant uses a standardized protocol across a large compound library.

Moderate lipophilicity (logP 1-4) provides the driving force for membrane partitioning. Molecular weight < 500 Da. Intramolecular hydrogen bonds can "mask" polar groups and improve permeability beyond what TPSA alone would predict — this is exploited in cyclic peptide drug design. Compact, low-flexibility conformations reduce the entropic cost of membrane insertion.

Features associated with poor PAMPA permeability: high TPSA (>120 Å²) is the dominant negative predictor. Multiple hydrogen bond donors (HBD ≥ 4) strongly reduce permeability. Charged species at the assay pH (typically pH 7.4) — carboxylates, phosphates, quaternary amines — have very poor passive diffusion because the charge cannot be buried in the lipid interior.
